subject: ALGEBRA 1
pageTitle: Percent Change Formula: Increase, Decrease and the Base Trap
description: Calculate percent increase and decrease with (new − old) / old, and see why going up 25% and back down is not 25%, with two worked examples.
caption: Percent change in 7 swipes: the formula, increase vs decrease, and the base trap. Save this for your next algebra quiz. Free Algebra I study guide at precisstudy.com/algebra1 (no sign-up).

slides.title: PERCENT CHANGE: DON'T DIVIDE BY THE WRONG NUMBER
THE FORMULA
slides.note: A positive answer is an increase; a negative answer is a decrease.

slides.title: THE BASE IS ALWAYS THE OLD VALUE
lines: Going up: divide by the smaller starting number
Going down: divide by the larger starting number

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: A price rises from $40 to $50. What is the percent increase?

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: The price then drops from $50 back to $40. What is the percent decrease?

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Up 25% then down 25% gets you back
points: The second percent uses a different base.
Always divide by the starting value of that step.
